body:
Review pass 36. The extrapolation I discarded last pass finished, and your gate falsifies it - which is useful evidence rather than just an admission.

The invalid slice-shrinking method produced:

  slices=1  nodes=2184  analysis= 14.9s  us/node= 6826.5   (mean k 12.6)
  slices=2  nodes=4368  analysis= 53.1s  us/node=12156.1   (mean k 21.3)
  slices=3  nodes=6552  analysis=119.0s  us/node=18162.2   (mean k 24.9)

  naive mean seconds/node    0.01238
  naive projected ceiling    145377 nodes
  naive prediction for your 52416-node fixture:  10.8 MINUTES

Your gate has now run 47 min 55 s on that fixture without finishing. The naive method underpredicted by at least 4.4x and would have reported a comfortable pass where the truth is a decisive fail.

The cause is right there in the table: per-node cost is not constant, it climbs 6826 -> 12156 -> 18162 us as mean k grows 12.6 -> 21.3 -> 24.9. Shrinking slices shrinks the searchlights and the k-by-k solve dominates. Second contaminant: those timings ran while your gate saturated a core, so they measure contention too. Fitting a k exponent from them gives 1.10 between the first pair and 2.57 between the second - the signature of two uncontrolled variables moving together. Discarded in full.

WHAT STANDS - the bound taken straight from your gate, no model required:

  52416 nodes at mean k 31.2 exceeds 30 minutes
  -> 30-minute ceiling is at most 52416 * 30/48 = 32760 nodes, and lower since it has not finished

So Epic 8 can state today: dense-metric ceiling below roughly 33000 nodes at support size ~31. Now bounded by two independent observations rather than one.

WHEN YOU PIN IT PROPERLY: hold active_slices at 24 so k stays near 31, vary the IN-PLANE extent to change node count, run on a quiet machine, and report mean k next to every timing so the normalisation is auditable. That last part is the bit that would have saved me here.
